title: More than a likeness
lines: Anatomy of an Echo asks who may continue a life that others recognize.
A familiar face can reassure a family before anyone agrees what that resemblance permits.
This science fiction novel follows a potter whose partner faces a clinic's promise of continuation.
It joins an intimate investigation with a harder question about who controls the resulting lives.
Read it for the tension between recognizing someone and accepting their claim on a relationship.

title: The bowl that listened
lines: Mara's bowl leans after firing, and the workshop intelligence recommends recycling it.
She keeps the bowl while Elias repairs a sensor the system could simply replace.
Their jokes and shared work establish what a promise of preservation might miss.
A medical warning interrupts the repair and brings Elias toward the Continuity clinic.
There, another advanced treatment is tied to completing his digital continuation.
Care and pressure occupy the same conversation, making refusal more complicated than a signature.

title: A message arrives early
lines: Before final modeling should begin, Elias receives a recording of his younger likeness.
The recorded figure warns him against completing Continuity.
His familiar hand gesture appears both in the recording and beside Mara.
Recognition makes the message disturbing, but cannot establish who or what produced it.
The investigation leads toward institutions that can classify a speaking instance or interrupt it.
The novel asks how much that control decides before its categories have been justified.

title: Read before deciding
lines: Partners, children, doctors, and Echoes bring different needs to the promise of more time.
The story keeps those claims personal without settling consciousness through a convenient definition.
Begin with The Bowl That Listened, then follow the unexpected recording into the clinic's claims.
Attend to who consents, who can refuse, and who controls the conditions of speaking.
Read the novel to question what a likeness may ask of the people who remain.
